name: Hrotsvit of Gandersheim
credit: Albrecht Dürer, woodcut of Hrotsvit presenting her book to Otto I, from Conrad Celtes's 1501 edition · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Hrotsvit (also Hrotsvitha or Roswitha) of Gandersheim was a Saxon canoness who lived and wrote in the abbey of Gandersheim in the second half of the tenth century. She is the first known woman writer of the German lands and the first Western writer since antiquity to compose drama; she also wrote Latin verse legends and historical poems in praise of the Ottonian dynasty.

Her six plays, in rhymed Latin prose, were written as Christian answers to the comedies of Terence, whose style she admired but whose subjects she wished to replace with the triumph of chastity and faith. They were rediscovered in a Regensburg manuscript by the humanist Conrad Celtes, who printed them in 1501 with woodcuts by Albrecht Dürer.
